collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The elders have blocked a plan the young villagers want: protest, or try again with a better plan.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The young villagers want to build a new fish pond, and the elders have said no, without much explanation. (friend) is angry: the elders always say no. (subject), one of the elders, actually thinks the pond is a good idea, but was outvoted. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The young villagers sit outside the elders' hut for a whole day. The elders are annoyed. (subject) comes out and tells them the real reason: the pond site floods. The protest turns into a meeting about a better site.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) goes to (subject) for advice, and together they redraw the plan: a smaller pond, on higher ground, with the elders' old fish trap as part of it. The elders approve it. (friend) is still annoyed they had to try twice.
